newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -BUND VOL STEADY, BUT EXPECTED TO BLIP UP.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -BUND VOL STEADY, BUT EXPECTED TO BLIP UP.

text.p: Implied volatility of Bund options was broadly steady on Monday but put trades dominated activity and dealers expected volatility to spike higher.

Bund futures held up well despite a fallout in Treasuries on Friday as investors turned increasingly nervous about a robust growth in the U.S. economy in the second quarter, and the possible effects on inflation.
But traders said the market was nervous about any repercussions on volatility from U.S. July retail sales data on Wednesday and the Bundesbank's decision on repo rates on Tuesday.
"It will start getting busier. I think volatility will start picking up tomorrow. At the moment there is no data," said one trader at a U.S. bank.

British brokers said the most active September 102.00 at-the-money strike was quoted at around 5.35-5.45 percent volatility, almost unchanged from Friday's close but slightly higher than the intra-day level of around 5.31 percent.
By 1205 GMT, September Bund futures were up 18 basis points on the day to 101.93, off their earlier high of 101.98.

One U.S. house was said to have sold 1,000 contracts of put spreads at 101.50-102.00 strikes at the opening. On the put side the most aggressive trades were in 101.50 which saw 2,500 lots change hands. There were also some 1,500 lots traded at the 101.00 strike, almost 2,000 at 102.00 and 1,600 at 102.50, traders said.
"People are still buying puts quite aggressively," said the U.S. bank trader.
"Buyers are anticipating the volatility to spike up again and obviously people are concerned about what happened on Friday," he said.
September call activity was clustered around the 102.00 strike.
"September is a fairly cheap trade that covers you for the whole week," said the trader.
September options will expire on August 21.

The Bundesbank will set its next repo tender on Tuesday, amid speculation it will switch to a variable rate repo and allow money market rates to rise. But the mark has recovered from last week's nearly eight-year lows against the dollar, and analysts reckon that unless it hits 1.90 to the dollar a Buba move is unlikely.
The dollar/mark stood at 1.8563 at European midday.
